title: TAVR Changed Valve Replacement; Anteris Says Longer-Living Patients Expose the Next Challenge
summary: For more than two decades, transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has been celebrated as one of cardiovascular medicine's great procedural success stories. It made valve replacement possible for patients once considered too high-risk for open-heart surgery, accelerated recovery times, and helped build a multibillion-dollar structural heart market. But a harder question is now emerging: if the valve is implanted successfully, does that mean the patient has been restored to health?
